equity_bridge.note: PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansLiabilitiesNoncurrent $697M at 2025-12-31 (FY2025 10-K XBRL) x (1 - 25%). Gross liability side only; surplus plans not netted (conservative).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All historical CAGRs are merger artefacts and are NOT used. FY2022-23 = legacy Smurfit Kappa only (~$12-13.5B revenue); FY2024 = ~6-month WestRock stub; FY2025 = first full combined year ($31.2B). Revenue and equity CAGRs (32%, 39-51%) measure the all-share acquisition of WestRock; EPS CAGR (-31%) measures the doubled share count (260M -> 526M) and purchase-accounting D&A step-up. Owner-FCF CAGR uses FY2022 $435M (503 - 68 SBC; equity-award taxes nil) -> FY2025 $992M. Equity 5yr is FY2021->FY2025 (4 years; FY2020 not in the CSV). Selected 3.0% = management's medium-term market growth (~1.6% NA, ~1.7% Europe, ~2.0% LatAm) plus ~1pp price/mix.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted FCF CAGR (31.6%) vs reported FCF CAGR FY2022-25 (503 -> 1,200 = 33.6%): SBC plus withholding taxes went from $68M to $208M, i.e. the WestRock plan and post-merger awards are growing faster than cash flow, but at 0.67% of revenue the gap is small.

scenario_narratives.base: The merger thesis half-works. FY2026 lands at the cut $4.9-5.1B guide as freight (~$300M) and input inflation (~$300M) absorb the early-2026 price gains; the $100/t NA increase for 2027 and the >$400M synergy run-rate lift EBITDA margins ~80bps in 2027, and network closures (Birmingham, UK/NL converting, NA box plants) carry the margin to ~17.3% by 2030 -- about $6.3B EBITDA against management's ~$7B. Volume grows with the market (~1.6-2.0%) plus modest price. Deleveraging toward <2.0x proceeds, buybacks start late 2027, but containerboard remains a price-taking cyclical and margins settle at a 17% through-cycle level. Terminal at 16x unlevered owner FCF (~5.8x EBITDA) assumes no re-rating above today's ~7x EV/EBITDA.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management's medium-term plan is delivered in full: the tight 2026 market ('nearly sold out' on most grades) carries the $100/t increase into 2027, freight normalises, North America's 'full potential' (WestRock mill reliability, mix) closes the margin gap to legacy Smurfit Kappa, and EBITDA reaches ~$7B (~19%) by 2030 with ~$14B of discretionary FCF funding dividends and buybacks. Plastic-to-fibre substitution and EU PPWR add ~0.5pp/yr of volume. Through-cycle margin settles at 18.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 tightening proves temporary: new NA recycled-containerboard capacity and a consumer slowdown reverse pricing in 2027 (revenue -1%), European demand stays weak, and the cost inflation that forced the August-2026 guidance cut becomes structural. Margins sit at the FY2025 ~15% level for a decade, synergies are competed away to customers, and with ~2.9x net debt/EBITDA buybacks never start. The business survives comfortably (investment grade, no refinancing wall) -- this is an earnings bear, not a solvency bear.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF on the first full post-merger year. The thesis is margin, not growth: the market is ~2% volume growth and a price-taking commodity, so value turns on whether the combined network earns a 17% (base) or 19% (management) through-cycle EBITDA margin. Pre-merger history is unusable for growth; it is used only as a margin reference (legacy Smurfit Kappa earned ~16-19%). Heavy leverage ($13.5B net debt against ~$22B equity) makes equity value roughly 1.6x geared to enterprise value -- every $1B of EV is ~$1.90/share.
key_risks_to_valuation: Containerboard pricing: each 1pp of through-cycle EBITDA margin is ~$0.3B/yr of EBITDA and roughly $5-6/share
Leverage gearing: net debt ~60% of market cap amplifies any EV error into equity
Guidance credibility: FY2026 was cut once in August 2026 on freight and input costs
Capex: guidance excludes ~$4B of growth capex; if it is spent without return, FCF is overstated
Pension and restructuring: closures are recurring; the 0.5%-of-revenue allowance may be light in a downturn

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average 526M (Q2 2026 10-Q, also FY2025 10-K); cover-page basic 524.5M at 2026-07-24. Held FLAT: SBC (incl. equity-award withholding taxes) is expensed in the flows. Buybacks only start in 2027 per the Feb-2026 medium-term plan, so the flat count is currently a modelling convention the company has not yet paid for.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow SBC add-back $139M + $69M taxes paid on net-share settlement (no combined reconciliation figure used; summed). Interest income ($111M FY2025) NOT stripped: company is net debt, not net cash.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.25% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta 1.2 (containerboard peers IP/PKG ~1.0-1.2, plus merger leverage) -> CoE 10.25%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (FY2025 interest expense $840M on ~$14B debt = 6.0% incl. fees; marginal IG issuance ~5.3-5.6%), after 25% tax ~4.1%. Market weights: equity ~$22.4B (526M x price), net debt $13.5B -> D/V ~38%. WACC = 0.62x10.25 + 0.38x4.1 = 7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows, not in a rate premium (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), as US GAAP delivers it: operating-lease cost ($1.1B operating lease liabilities FY2025) sits inside EBITDA and operating lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases (~$550M) are inside total_debt and their cost below EBITDA. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial ($24M at 2026-06-30) -- deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are consolidated.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with mid-cycle margin treatment (routing: cyclical operating company -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Smurfit Westrock is a vertically integrated containerboard/corrugated manufacturer, an operating company whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; it is cyclical, capital-intensive and leveraged, so the margin path is a through-cycle path (not FY2025 trough, not management's 2030 target carried forward) and the terminal cap is low. BASE YEAR: FY2025 is the first full combined year after the 5-Jul-2024 Smurfit Kappa/WestRock merger; FY2021-23 are legacy Smurfit Kappa only and FY2024 is a ~6-month WestRock stub, so NO pre-merger growth rate is used anywhere in the projection. EBITDA DEFINITION: the margin path is pre-SBC EBITDA excluding impairments and merger/integration one-offs but AFTER a recurring ~0.5%-of-revenue cash restructuring allowance (closures are a permanent feature of a mill network). FY2025 anchor: GAAP EBITDA (op income + D&A) $4,269M + SBC $139M + restructuring & impairment charges $385M = $4,793M (15.4%), less ~$150M recurring restructuring cash = ~14.9%. FY2026 guidance $4.9-5.1B adjusted EBITDA (cut in Aug-26 for a ~$300M freight headwind and ~$300M input inflation) on ~$32.1B revenue (H1 $15.7B actual) is ~15.6% adjusted, ~15.2% on this definition. Year-1 owner-FCF sanity: ~$1.0B unlevered-after-SBC vs FY2025 reported owner FCF $992M after ~$800M net interest -- the unlevered build adds back interest, consistent. Net debt is the 30-Jun-2026 10-Q (debt $14,164M incl. finance leases, cash $677M). Pension: $697M non-current pension/OPEB liability (FY2025 10-K) deducted net of 25% tax in the bridge. Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF $1,200M (OCF $3,392M - capex $2,192M) - SBC incl. equity-award taxes $208M = $992M.

bear.margin_rationale: 2027 price increase fails to stick, new NA capacity and a soft consumer cycle push containerboard back to 2025 'pretty bad' conditions; margins stuck at the FY2025 level (~15%) for the decade as synergies are competed away. Capex does not fall (mill base must be maintained).

base.margin_rationale: FY2026 at guidance midpoint less recurring restructuring (15.2%); the $100/t 2027 NA price platform and synergy run-rate lift 2027 to 16%; reaches 17.3% by 2030, ~200bps short of management's ~19% (~$7B) target, then fades to a 17.0% through-cycle level. Base deliberately does not credit the full 2030 target: it assumes peak-ish containerboard pricing that a cyclical will not hold through the cycle.
base.capex_rationale: Guidance $2.4-2.8B/yr 2026-30 excludes ~$4B growth capex; 7.6% of revenue = $2.5-2.8B over the plan. D&A glides to 7.6% so terminal capex = terminal D&A (purchase-accounting intangible amortization rolls off).

bull.margin_rationale: Management's plan delivered: ~$7B EBITDA on ~$38B revenue by 2030 (~19%), $100/t holds into 2027, freight normalises; through-cycle fade only to 18.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): FY2026 guidance was already cut once, leverage is ~2.9x vs a <2.0x target, and containerboard pricing is a commodity cycle that was 'pretty bad' as recently as 2025. Base 50%: the synergy delivery to date (>$400M ahead of schedule) is evidence the integration is on track. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs several independent things at once -- the $100/t increase sticking, freight normalising, and NA mill performance converging on legacy Smurfit Kappa.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
